verdict.rationale: Jitsu documents a first-party webhook destination that sends event data to any HTTP endpoint. Connecting a source to a destination, plus Functions, lets users choose which events are delivered, so a programmatic consumer can subscribe to the event stream. The evidence is a single short doc line with no detail on delivery semantics, and there is no hands-on corroboration. Missing for 10: documented payload format, signing/authentication of callbacks, retry/delivery guarantees for the webhook destination, event-type subscription granularity beyond filtering, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can subscribe to events via webhooks

citations.quote: Send data to any HTTP endpoint. You can use this destination to send data to Slack, Discord, or any other service that accepts HTTP requests.
You can control which events become active by choosing not to connect a source to a destination or by using a Jitsu Function to filter out unwanted events before they are sent.
